record.original_question: Is every compact sequential space of character ω1, or even of cardinality ω1, hereditarily α-realcompact, where a space is α-realcompact if every countably complete ultrafilter of closed sets is fixed?

evidence.quote: Question 17. Is every compact sequential space of character (or cardinality) ω1 hereditarily α-realcompact?
Nyikos deﬁnes a space to be α-realcompact if every countably complete ultraﬁlter of closed sets is ﬁxed.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A topological space $X$ is called α-realcompact if every countably complete ultrafilter of closed subsets of $X$ is fixed (i.e., has nonempty intersection); equivalently, every maximal family of closed sets with the countable intersection property has nonempty intersection. A space is hereditarily α-realcompact if every subspace of it is α-realcompact. A space $X$ is sequential if a subset $A \subseteq X$ is closed whenever it contains the limit of every convergent sequence from $A$. The character of $X$ is the smallest cardinal $\kappa$ such that every point of $X$ has a neighborhood base of size at most $\kappa$.

Question: Is every compact sequential Hausdorff space of character $\omega_1$ hereditarily α-realcompact? More restrictively, is every compact sequential Hausdorff space of cardinality $\omega_1$ hereditarily α-realcompact?
artifact.status_search_result: Related work by Nyikos shows that under the axiom ♣ there exists a compact sequential space of nonmeasurable cardinality that fails to be hereditarily α-realcompact, but a complete ZFC resolution of whether every compact sequential space of character (or cardinality) $\omega_1$ is hereditarily α-realcompact does not appear in the located sources. Current status is unclear.
